objectives.text: DESCRIBE the operating characteristics of a lead-acid battery to include methods of voltage production, state of charge, and hazards associated with storage batteries.

enabling.text: DEFINE the following terms as they relate to batteries and voltaic cells:
STATE the purpose of a battery.
DESCRIBE the operation of a simple voltaic cell.
STATE the chemical equation for the reaction that occurs when a lead-acid battery is being charged or discharged.
EXPLAIN the relationship between specific gravity and state of charge of a lead-acid battery.
DESCRIBE the relationship between total battery voltage and cell voltage for a series-connected battery.
STATE the advantage of connecting a battery in parallel with respect to current-carrying capability.
STATE the difference between primary and secondary cells with respect to recharge capability.
STATE the advantage of each of the following types of batteries:
EXPLAIN the adverse effects of a shorted cell.
EXPLAIN how gas generation is minimized for a lead-acid battery.
EXPLAIN how heat is generated in a lead-acid battery.

passages.quote: The term voltaic cell is defined as a combination of materials used to convert chemical energy into electrical energy.
A battery is a group of two or more connected voltaic cells.
An electrode is a metallic compound, or metal, which has an abundance of electrons (negative electrode) or an abundance of positive charges (positive electrode).
An electrolyte is a solution which is capable of conducting an electric current.
Specific gravity is defined as the ratio comparing the weight of any liquid to the weight of an equal volume of water.
Specific gravity is measured with a hydrometer.
An ampere-hour is defined as a current of one ampere flowing for one hour.
The purpose of a battery is to store chemical energy and to convert this chemical energy into electrical energy when the need arises.
a chemical cell (or voltaic cell) consists of two electrodes of different types of metals or metallic compounds and an electrolyte solution
The positive plate consists of lead peroxide (PbO2), and the negative plate is sponge lead (Pb)
Since hydrogen is highly explosive, it is necessary to provide adequate ventilation to the battery whenever charging is in progress.
the value of specific gravity at any given time is an approximate indication of the battery’s state of charge.
The specific gravity decreases as the battery discharges and increases to its normal, original value as it is charged.
it will increase the current-carrying capability of the
Cells that cannot be returned to good condition, or recharged after their voltage output has dropped to a value that is not usable, are called primary cells.
Cells that can be recharged to nearly their original condition are called secondary cells.
The capacity of a storage battery determines how long the storage battery will operate at a certain discharge rate and is rated in ampere-hours.
internal resistance reduces both the current and voltage available to the load.
The shelf life of a battery is the time which a battery may be stored and not lose more than 10 percent of its original capacity.
The output voltage of a battery connected in series is equal to the sum of the cell
The advantage of a carbon-zinc battery is that it is durable and very inexpensive to produce.
The alkaline cell has the advantage of an extended life over that of a carbon-zinc cell of the same size
The nickel-cadmium battery has the advantage of being a dry cell that is a true storage battery with a reversible chemical reaction
The edison cell has the advantage of being a lighter and more rugged secondary cell than a lead-acid storage battery.
has the advantage of maintaining a fairly constant output under varying load conditions.
With each shorted cell, battery capacity is reduced by a percentage equal to one over the total number of cells.
Overcharging and overdischarging should be avoided at all costs.
To reduce the amount of gassing, charging voltages above 2.30 volts per cell should be minimized
the current flowing through the battery will cause heat to be generated by the electrolysis of water.
Very high temperatures, 125°F and higher, can actually do damage to the battery and cause early failure.

body.text: If the electrolyte is a paste, the cell is a dry cell. If it is a solution, the cell is a wet cell.
Lead-acid batteries use an electrolyte that contains sulfuric acid. The specific gravity of the electrolyte falls between 1.000 and 1.835, and it is normally mixed to be less than 1.350.

body.alt: A hydrometer: a rubber bulb on a glass tube holding a weighted glass float with a scale along its body.

o: A metal with an abundance of electrons
A solution capable of conducting an electric current
A group of connected voltaic cells
A measure of current over time
checks.x: An electrolyte is a solution which is capable of conducting an electric current.

checks.q: A current of 5 amps flows for 20 hours. How many ampere-hours is this?
checks.x: Multiply the current in amperes by the time of flow in hours: 5 x 20 = 100 ampere-hours.

checks.q: A battery stores chemical energy so that it can be converted into what?
checks.x: The purpose of a battery is to store chemical energy and to convert it into electrical energy when the need arises.

body.text: In a cell with zinc and copper electrodes, the zinc electrode accumulates a much larger negative charge because it dissolves into the electrolyte.

body.cap: Basic Chemical Production of Electrical Power
body.alt: Two views of a cell with zinc and copper electrodes in an electrolyte, showing positive and negative ions moving between them.

body.text: Electrons are removed from the copper electrode, leaving it with an excess of positive charge.
If a load is connected across the electrodes, free electrons in the negative zinc electrode move through the wire and load toward the positive copper electrode.
The potential difference that results allows the cell to function as a source of applied voltage.

checks.q: What does a voltaic cell consist of?
o: Two electrodes of different metals or metallic compounds and an electrolyte solution
Two electrodes of the same metal in air
A coil of wire and a permeable core
Two metal plates separated by a dielectric
checks.x: A chemical or voltaic cell consists of two electrodes of different types of metals or metallic compounds and an electrolyte solution.

body.text: Two types of lead are acted upon electro-chemically by a solution of diluted sulfuric acid.
On discharge, the electrolyte divides, its hydrogen combines with oxygen to produce water, and the sulfate combines with the lead of both plates to form lead sulphate.
Discharge: PbO2 + Pb + 2H2SO4 → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O

body.alt: A lead-acid cell on discharge connected to a load, with both plates changing to lead sulfate and the electrolyte becoming weaker.

body.text: On charge, the action is reversed, and the return of acid to the electrolyte increases the specific gravity.
Charge: PbO2 + Pb + 2H2SO4 ← 2PbSO4 + 2H2O

body.alt: A lead-acid cell on charge connected to a charger, with the plates changing back to lead peroxide and sponge lead.

body.cap: Voltage and Specific Gravity During Charge and Discharge
body.alt: Graph of cell voltage and specific gravity against time during discharge and charge. Specific gravity falls in a straight line on discharge and rises unevenly on charge.

body.text: The decrease in specific gravity on discharge is proportional to the ampere-hours discharged. The rise while charging is not uniform.

checks.q: What do the plates of a lead-acid battery form on discharge?
checks.x: The sulfate combines with the lead of both plates, forming lead sulphate.

checks.q: What happens to specific gravity as a lead-acid battery discharges?
checks.x: The specific gravity decreases as the battery discharges and increases to its normal, original value as it is charged.

body.text: In a series connection, the positive terminal of one cell is connected to the negative terminal of the next. Four 1.5 V cells provide a total of 6 volts.

body.alt: Four 1.5 volt cells joined positive to negative, totaling 6 volts, with the schematic form below.

body.text: In a parallel connection, all the positive terminals are connected together and all the negative terminals are connected together. The total voltage is the same as that of a single cell.

body.alt: Three 1.5 volt cells with their positive terminals joined and their negative terminals joined, with the schematic form below.

Dry cells in flashlights are examples of primary cells. The most common secondary cell is the lead-acid automobile battery.
Internal resistance is due mainly to the resistance of the electrolyte between electrodes.

checks.q: Six 1.5 volt cells are connected in series. What is the battery voltage?
checks.x: The output voltage equals the sum of the cell voltages: 6 x 1.5 = 9 volts.

checks.q: What is the advantage of connecting cells in parallel?
checks.x: Connecting cells in parallel will increase the current-carrying capability of the battery. The voltage stays the same as a single cell.

o: Secondary cells can be recharged, and primary cells cannot
Primary cells can be recharged, and secondary cells cannot
Primary cells use a paste, and secondary cells use a liquid
Both can be recharged, but primary cells last longer
checks.x: Primary cells cannot be recharged. Secondary cells can be recharged to nearly their original condition.

checks.q: What is the advantage of a carbon-zinc cell?
o: It is durable and very inexpensive to produce
It keeps a constant output under varying loads
It is lighter than a lead-acid battery
checks.x: The advantage of a carbon-zinc battery is that it is durable and very inexpensive to produce.

checks.q: Which cell has the advantage of a fairly constant output under varying load conditions?
checks.x: The mercury cell has the advantage of maintaining a fairly constant output under varying load conditions.

checks.q: What advantage does the edison cell have over a lead-acid storage battery?

It has a higher cell voltage
checks.x: The edison cell has the advantage of being a lighter and more rugged secondary cell than a lead-acid storage battery.

body.text: Cell short circuits can be caused by faulty separators, metal particles forming a circuit between the plates, buckling of the plates, or excessive sediments in the bottom of the jar.
A lead-acid battery cannot absorb all the energy from the charging source near the completion of the charge. The excess energy produces hydrogen and oxygen. This process is known as gassing.
Gassing is first noticed when cell voltage reaches 2.30-2.35 volts per cell.
No smoking, electric sparks, or open flames are allowed near a charging battery.
The operating temperature of a battery should preferably be maintained in the nominal band of 60-80°F.
The current also generates heat as it passes through the internal resistance, during both charge and discharge.
P = I²Ri
Low temperatures lower battery capacity but prolong battery life under floating operation or storage.

checks.q: One cell of a six cell battery is shorted. By what fraction is battery capacity reduced?
checks.x: With each shorted cell, capacity is reduced by a percentage equal to one over the total number of cells: 1/6.

checks.q: How is the amount of gassing reduced in a lead-acid battery?
o: By minimizing charging voltages above 2.30 volts per cell
checks.x: To reduce the amount of gassing, charging voltages above 2.30 volts per cell should be minimized.

checks.q: Which two effects generate heat in a lead-acid battery during charging?
o: Electrolysis of water and current through the internal resistance
checks.x: Current causes heat through the electrolysis of water, and also as it passes through the internal resistance (I²Ri).

examples.title: State of charge from specific gravity
examples.problem: A lead-acid battery reads 1.175 specific gravity. Its full charge specific gravity is 1.260, and it has a normal gravity drop of 120 points. Estimate its state of charge.
steps: Fully charged 1.260 minus present charge 1.175 is 85 points.
The battery is 85 points below its fully charged state, out of a 120 point drop.

summary.text: A voltaic cell converts chemical energy into electrical energy, and a battery is two or more connected voltaic cells.
Specific gravity of a lead-acid battery decreases proportionally during discharge, so it is an approximate indication of state of charge.
A battery connected in series has an output voltage equal to the sum of the cell voltages. One connected in parallel has a greater current-carrying capability.
Secondary cells can be recharged, and primary cells cannot.
Short circuits cause a great reduction in battery capacity.
If gassing occurs and the gases are allowed to collect, an explosive mixture of hydrogen and oxygen can be produced.
Charging current generates heat by the electrolysis of water and by I²Ri.
